dedupe_keys.name: spotgeo dataset esa kelvins spot the geo satellites challenge

description: The spotGEO dataset contains 6,400 sequences of five grayscale 640 by 480 pixel images, 32,000 frames in all, from low-cost optical ground sensors at several locations, with annotations of the positions of geostationary objects in each frame. ESA's Advanced Concepts Team built it with the University of Adelaide for the Kelvins Spot the GEO Satellites challenge, run from June to September 2020, to find algorithms that detect faint GEO objects despite clouds, weather, light pollution, sensor noise and star occlusions. Coverage is the geostationary belt as seen from the observation sites; the training part is labelled and the test part is not. Format and access: PNG frames with JSON annotations in a ZIP of about 4.2 GB; version 2.0 with additional annotations was released on Zenodo in January 2021, with a starter kit. Licence: CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: a benchmark for detection algorithms, not an operational catalogue, and the labels come from the organisers. It supports calibration and validation of low-cost space surveillance used in hazard exposure studies of the GEO belt. Related catalogue records are the ESA collision avoidance challenge dataset and the CelesTrak GP and SATCAT data.
